ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against: (i) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (Global Affairs Canada) issued under SEMA and the Magnitsky Law; (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Consolidated Sanctions Lists; (iv) Interpol and other counter-terrorism watchlists; and (v) domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEP) databases (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones, LexisNexis Bridger, or equivalent) using a risk-based approach. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory upon any PEP designation, sanctions match, negative adverse-media finding, or high-risk-country nexus. Screening results must be documented, retained for at least five years per PCMLTFA record-keeping requirements, and refreshed annually or upon any change in ownership or control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Online Services (Services en ligne) at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; CLIC filing platform for enterprise naming, reservation, and incorporation filings
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, every legal person constituted in Quebec must have a corporate name in French. The French form is the primary registered legal name; an English or other-language version may be added only if an exception applies (e.g., recognized registered trademark or statutorily exempt sector). Names derived from a non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese characters) must be transliterated phonetically into French/Latin characters with appropriate French diacritics. The enterprise name must include a distinctive element, a descriptive element (optional), an indicia of legal form (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Société par actions'), must not be misleading, misleadingly similar to an existing enterprise name, or violate a reserved professional title.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Loan and Finance / Prêt et finance (regulated lending token)
Engineer / Ingénieur (reserved by the Professional Code, CQLR c. C-26)
Chartered Professional Accountant / Comptable professionnel agréé (reserved title)
Lawyer / Avocat and Notary / Notaire (reserved professional titles)
Québec, Montréal, or any municipal or regional toponym (requires consent or may be impermissible)
International / Internationale or Canadian / Canadien if geographically misleading
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name-rejection notice from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec: (1) obtain the written statement of grounds for refusal; (2) correct the proposed name by adding a distinctive element, removing prohibited tokens, conforming to French-language transliteration and Charter of the French Language requirements, or appending a certified copy of a registered trademark where the refusal relates to a trademark exception; (3) resubmit an amended name reservation through the REQ online portal within the remaining reservation window, or file a fresh reservation with a new distinctive element; (4) if the Registraire maintains the refusal, file a written administrative review application addressed to the Registrar within 30 days of the refusal notice, annexing the REQ preliminary name-search certificate, supporting trademark registrations, evidence of French-language compliance, and any legal opinion from Quebec counsel; (5) if the administrative review is unsuccessful, contest the refusal before the Court of Québec within the applicable statutory time period per the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), following the ordinary civil procedure for judicial contestation; and (6) concurrently instruct Quebec counsel to prepare a secondary preferred name to avoid operational delay. Professional legal fees for an appeal are typically not statutory and are borne by the applicant.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services providing only a mailing address are not permissible as the statutory registered office (siége social) for a licensed dangerous-goods battery safety testing laboratory in Quebec. The registered office must be a physical location in Quebec where the enterprise's records, management, and statutory documents can be reached and where process may be served. A commercial virtual address may be used solely as an auxiliary mailing address. Given the UN 38.3 testing scope (drop, shock, vibration, thermal, and electrical abuse testing of lithium batteries), the enterprise must maintain dedicated physical operational premises compliant with Quebec occupational health and safety (CNESST), fire code, building code, and environmental requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - quantified annual probability of 75% (confidence band 60-90%) of at least one unannounced on-site inspection by competent authorities, including municipal fire safety services, CNESST inspectors, ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation body surveillance assessors (e.g., Standards Council of Canada or recognized accreditation body), and Transport Canada officials verifying dangerous-goods test procedures and record-keeping.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c. S-31.1, Part II (Incorporation), as amended; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs) together with the declaration of registration under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed. One or more incorporators may subscribe for shares; consideration may be cash, property, or past services; no escrow account or paid-up capital deposit is required under the Business Corporations Act (Quebec).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the resolutions of the first board of directors of the Corporation, as follows: 1. The share subscription list submitted by the sole incorporator is approved, and one hundred common shares are issued to the subscriber for lawful consideration, which consideration is hereby accepted as fully paid. 2. The registered office is adopted at 1000, rue de la Gauchetiere Ouest, Montreal, Quebec H3B 4W5; corporate books and records shall be maintained there. 3. The individuals identified in the appointment minutes are elected as President, Secretary and Treasurer, respectively, each to serve until a successor is appointed. Any two officers may execute banking and business instruments on behalf of the Corporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, online name-reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three ranked proposed corporate names through the Registraire's online portal or the official paper form. The name must be distinctive, lawful, and not contrary to public order. Wait for the certificate of reservation, which is valid for 120 days, before filing the articles.
required_dossiers: Written authorization if filed by a representative or attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a new reservation request with distinct, admissible name elements; no automatic extension is granted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel or a notary in Quebec, followed by online submission to Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation containing the corporate name, registered office address, share structure, restrictions on activities, and initial directors. Execute the articles before two witnesses or in accordance with the electronic signature protocol. Attach the name reservation certificate and any required declarations.
required_dossiers: Identification documents for incorporators and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise any deficient clauses and re-execute the articles; apply online to resume processing; additional statutory fees may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and Payment of Incorporation Filing to Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises - Mon Dossier / Entreprises Quebec online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a digital dossier, upload the executed articles and supporting declarations, confirm the fee payment, and submit the package electronically. Print and preserve the system acknowledgement and date-stamped receipt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct validation errors flagged by the portal and re-submit; the effective registration date is the date of the completed filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate and Assumption of Corporate Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After substantive review, the Registrar issues the certificate of constitution and registers the enterprise under the legal publicity regime, assigning a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). Obtain a certified copy of the certificate and record the corporate existence in the minute book.
required_dossiers: Acknowledged evidence of the accepted filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of intention to refuse, respond with corrected articles within the stated deadline or file an amended declaration; failure to cure will require a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); local municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a federal Business Number with the CRA and apply for any required GST/HST account and payroll accounts. Update the Registraire if director addresses or officers change. Open a corporate bank account using the certified certificate and board resolution, and maintain the statutory registers and minute book.
required_dossiers: Direct identity and background information for bank and CRA purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the account registration, provide a corrected business information return; if the Registraire asks for updated declarations, file the applicable declaration form electronically within the prescribed response period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministere de l'Economie, de l'Innovation et de l'Energie (MEIE) for industrial designation; Standards Council of Canada (SCC) for testing-laboratory accreditation; local municipal building/occupancy office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: ISO/IEC 17025 Accreditation for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (SCC) and municipal occupancy permit for a laboratory

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Declaration de conformite) for a low-impact physical and electromagnetic testing laboratory; full environmental impact assessment is not required when operations are limited to sealed-battery mechanical testing, temperature cycling, and electromagnetic compatibility testing without chemical processing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater may be discharged to a watercourse; floor drains must comply with municipal sewer by-laws. Any VOC or other air contaminants must meet the limits of the Quebec Clean Air Regulation (Q-2, r.4.1). Damaged and spent battery cells must be handled, stored, labeled, and shipped as hazardous materials under the Regulation respecting hazardous materials (Q-2, r.35) and the federal Transport of Dangerous Goods Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the competent municipal fire service under the Quebec Fire Safety Act and the Quebec Construction Code; structural load inspection and load-calculation certificate by a licensed engineer for the drop-test apparatus; CNESST occupational health and safety clearance for laboratory operations, including machine guarding, emergency eyewash, hazardous-products training, and confined-space protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online portals, administers the federal business number, corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and information-return programs. Revenu Quebec administers Quebec income tax for corporations, Quebec sales tax (QST), employer-source deductions, and related Quebec filings through clicSÉQUR and its online services. The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers customs export reporting through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under the Quebec Business Corporations Act and obtain the applicable certificate of incorporation and corporate registry number. 2. Apply to the CRA for a nine-digit Business Number (BN) through Business Registration Online or the applicable non-resident registration process. 3. Open the relevant CRA program accounts, including RC corporate income tax and RT GST/HST; payroll and information-return accounts are opened when applicable. 4. Register with Revenu Quebec for Quebec corporate income tax and, where required, QST, employer source deductions, and other Quebec tax programs. 5. Register for CERS access and obtain the required export reporting credentials if the entity exports commercial goods. 6. A non-resident corporation generally provides incorporation documents, legal name, registered address, directors, authorized representative information, business activities, fiscal year-end, Canadian activities, and supporting identity documents. GST/HST registration may be mandatory when the non-resident is carrying on commercial activities in Canada and exceeds the small-supplier threshold, and may be voluntary below the threshold. QST registration may be mandatory where the entity carries on business in Quebec and meets the applicable QST rules. There is no single Canadian VAT identification number; the GST/HST registration number is generally the BN followed by the RT program identifier, while a Quebec QST account is separately administered by Revenu Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general United States-style check-the-box election for corporations. A Canadian corporation is generally a separate taxpayer, while partnerships are generally fiscally transparent and trusts are subject to separate statutory rules. Available elections may include subsection 85(1) or 85(2) rollover elections for qualifying transfers of property to a corporation, section 86 share-reorganization elections, amalgamation and wind-up rules, functional-currency reporting elections for qualifying corporations, and specified GST/HST or QST elections. Canada has enacted hybrid-mismatch rules that can deny deductions or exempt amounts in specified cross-border arrangements; these are statutory anti-avoidance mechanisms rather than elective entity-classification elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST), with Quebec Sales Tax (QST) applying in Quebec. The combined ordinary Quebec consumption-tax burden is generally 14.975%, consisting of 5% GST and 9.975% QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, generally measured over the relevant single-quarter and preceding four-quarter periods, is the principal small-supplier threshold for GST/HST registration. Quebec generally applies a CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold for QST purposes, subject to statutory rules and special registration obligations. Certain non-resident suppliers, taxi and commercial ride services, and other specified businesses may be required to register under special rules. A business below the threshold may register voluntarily and must generally remain registered for the applicable minimum period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not generally require real-time electronic invoice clearance, government pre-approval, or digital tax stamping for ordinary domestic B2B supplies. Registrants must issue invoices containing prescribed GST/HST and QST information, maintain reliable electronic books and records, and retain supporting documents for the statutory retention period. CRA and Revenu Quebec generally permit electronic records and electronic filing. Certain tax returns, elections, payments, and information returns may be subject to mandatory electronic filing based on taxpayer category, filing volume, or statutory rules. Commercial exports are reported electronically to CBSA through CERS when reporting is required; CERS is a customs reporting platform and is not a VAT invoice-clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods may generally be zero-rated for GST and, where applicable, QST when supplied for export and the statutory export conditions are satisfied, including delivery or transfer outside Canada or Quebec and retention of documentary evidence that the goods were exported. Services supplied to a non-resident may qualify for zero-rating where the applicable statutory conditions are met, but exclusions apply, including services relating to Canadian real property, certain tangible personal property situated in Canada, litigation or dispute proceedings, and services performed in respect of goods or activities in Canada where the legislation excludes zero-rating. For a battery-safety and UN38.3 testing laboratory, testing performed in Canada for a non-resident customer is not automatically zero-rated; the customer status, contractual recipient, location and use of the testing, connection with Canadian goods or property, and all statutory exclusions must be reviewed. Input tax credits or QST input tax refunds generally require valid tax documentation and a direct connection with commercial activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) export declaration or other applicable CBSA export-reporting record
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, consignee, description, quantity, value, currency, terms of sale, and destination
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or other carrier transport document
Proof of export or delivery outside Canada, including carrier confirmation, customs exit evidence, or destination import documentation where available
Sales contract, purchase order, testing agreement, and customer records establishing the non-resident recipient and contractual scope
Certificate of origin or other origin document where required by the destination country or a trade agreement

Inward remittance or bank-payment evidence where relevant to commercial substantiation; Canadian GST/QST law does not impose a universal requirement for a specific inward-remittance certificate as a condition of zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general mandatory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds and no universal 180-day repatriation rule. CRA and Revenu Quebec may reassess GST/QST where zero-rating, input tax credits, or refunds are unsupported, including tax that should have been collected, denied credits or refunds, arrears interest, and applicable penalties. False statements or omissions may attract a penalty generally based on the tax understated or benefit overstated; gross-negligence penalties can generally be 50% of the relevant tax amount or benefit, subject to the governing statute. CRA may reassess beyond the ordinary limitation period in cases involving misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful blindness, or fraud. Fraudulent conduct may result in civil penalties and criminal prosecution, including fines and imprisonment. Incorrect or late export reporting may also trigger CBSA Administrative Monetary Penalties, seizure or detention consequences, and customs reassessment. Revenu Quebec applies comparable assessment, interest, penalty, and prosecution mechanisms for QST and Quebec tax violations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a freely floating exchange rate and full convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. No exchange control legislation restricts the inflow or outflow of capital, the repatriation of dividends, or the remittance of profits to non-resident shareholders. However, all cross-border electronic fund transfers of C$10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Banking documentation must articulate the source and purpose of funds for any large inbound remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian exporters are not required to surrender export proceeds or convert foreign currency receipts into Canadian dollars within any statutory timeline. Export proceeds may be held in any freely convertible currency. The only obligation is record-keeping and reporting under the PCMLTFA and the Income Tax Act for tax purposes, including the disclosure of foreign reporting entities and foreign bank accounts where applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-to-Medium as a supplementary payment rail only. Wise is registered in Canada as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and is permitted for low-value cross-border client payments, refunds, and vendor disbursements. However, Wise and other offshore Electronic Money Institutions are not chartered banks and do not offer Canadian Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) coverage. They cannot serve as the primary treasury clearing account for capital escrow, debt funding, or large trade settlements. An offshore EMI without a Canadian MSB registration is legally prohibited from actively soliciting or providing payment services to Canadian residents; it may only be used if the account is opened outside Canada with no Canadian nexus.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian Schedule I chartered banks permit remote corporate onboarding through video-verified identity attestation for signatories holding valid Canadian government-issued identification. Non-resident directors without Canadian identification will generally be required to attend an in-person interview at a bank branch or an authorized notary/consulate to execute the KYC certification. As a practical mandate, at least one director or senior officer with Canadian residential or business nexus must participate in either an in-person or video-interview session before the corporate account is activated. Foreign beneficial owners must provide certified passport copies, proof of address, and a board resolution attesting to the ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner or director is resident in, or connected to, a high-risk, sanctioned, or FATF grey-listed jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Obtain and submit: (1) current corporate registry extracts from the home jurisdiction, (2) notarized source-of-wealth declarations, (3) three years of audited financial statements or bank reference letters from a regulated financial institution, (4) a complete chain-of-title showing all intermediate entities between the ultimate beneficial owner and the Canadian entity, and (5) legal opinion from a qualified counsel confirming no sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial capital injection or capital contribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) board resolution authorizing the capital injection, (2) share subscription or shareholder loan agreement, (3) bank statements from the remitting account demonstrating provenance of funds, (4) audited financial statements or accountant's letter attesting to the financial capacity of the parent, and (5) tax clearances/certificates of residence for the parent entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire pattern inconsistent with stated business scope as a battery safety testing laboratory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (1) ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation certificate for UN38.3 drop testing and CE-RED electromagnetic compatibility testing, (2) fixed asset purchase agreements with equipment vendors, (3) client service contracts and shipping documents, (4) the company's compliance manual and transaction-monitoring procedures, and (5) a narrative business rationale for each major cross-border outflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a foreign electronic money institution (e.g., Wise) for repeated cross-border transactions without a documented treasury policy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (1) a board-approved treasury policy capping EMI transaction size and frequency, (2) FINTRAC MSB registration evidence for the EMI and confirmation of the EMI's Canadian licensing status, (3) a detailed ledger reconciling EMI transactions against client engagement letters and invoices, and (4) a transitional plan to migrate to a full SWIFT-supported chartered bank account as the primary clearing rail.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For foreign direct investment into the Quebec operating entity, the compliant routing is an inbound SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent or investor's bank to a Canadian dollar clearing account at a Schedule I bank. The payment must reference the purpose code 'Foreign Direct Investment in Canada' and include the beneficiary account name, the corporate account number, and a concise payment narrative such as 'Share subscription – Battery Safety UN38.3 Testing Lab Capital Escrow'. All inbound transfers of C$10,000 or more are subject to FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Reporting. The Canadian recipient bank will verify the source of funds and the underlying board resolution. For investments exceeding a prescribed threshold, additional documentation under the Investment Canada Act may be required if the transaction is notifiable; a thorough legal review should confirm whether Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada notification is necessary.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade settlements must be executed through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers using the primary Canadian bank account for high-value transactions. For purchases of precision test instruments and calibration equipment from overseas suppliers, a Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700 series) is the preferred clearing rail where the supplier requires payment assurance. Low-value recurring disbursements such as client refunds, calibration lab fees, or software subscriptions may be settled through Wise, subject to the board-approved treasury policy and FINTRAC compliance limits. All outbound wires must include proper purpose codes, underlying invoices or service contracts, and beneficial-owner information. Payments to sanctioned jurisdictions or persons are strictly prohibited.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Customized FX forwards with Canadian Schedule I banks for CAD/USD and CAD/EUR exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-convertible emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency swaps for long-term capital assets or intercompany loan exposures
Vanilla FX options (call/put) for balance-sheet hedging of foreign-currency receivables

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (federal Part I general rate 15.0% + Quebec general corporate rate 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED investment tax credit at 15% general rate (35% enhanced rate for qualifying CCPCs on the first CAD 3,000,000 of qualified expenditures); Quebec refundable RS-DE tax credit at 14% base rate and up to 30% for eligible SMEs in qualifying zones; federal small-business deduction reducing the federal rate to 9% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income of a CCPC, with Quebec's DPE reducing the provincial rate to approximately 3.2%-5.0% depending on the taxation year; accelerated capital cost allowance under Class 50/Class 54 (55%/45% declining balance) for electronic data-processing and laboratory automation equipment used in UN38.3 battery testing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the CRA NETFILE/E-file platform using certified tax software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal period-end; balance-due is payable within 2 months after year-end, or 3 months for an eligible CCPC claiming the small-business deduction

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 front page - Business Number (BN) and Taxation Year End
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA 15-character program-account code (RC0001 for federal corporate income tax) and the fiscal period-end date for the return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment (PE) must file a T2; indicate the Canadian PE province on the front page and complete Schedule 5A to allocate taxable income to Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Line 580 - Net income (loss) before taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial-statement net income before income taxes, reconciled to Canadian Part I tax accounting by adding back non-deductible items (50% of meals and entertainment, taxes on income, penalties) and deducting statutory allowances (CCA in lieu of book depreciation, exempt grants, and SR&ED current-expense deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source business income attributable to the Canadian PE; exclude foreign-source income not allocable to Canada and complete Schedule 21 for foreign accrual property income and treaty allocation refinements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for tax depreciation of UN38.3 drop-test rigs, thermal chambers, and transient laboratory instrumentation; Class 8 at 20% declining balance, Class 50 at 55% and Class 54 at 45% for electronic data-processing equipment, with accelerated investment incentive (AII) allowances available in the first year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CCA is confined to assets owned by and used in the Canadian PE; where the head office owns the equipment and the PE uses it, an arm's length rental or deemed capital cost is required, and intercompany use must be priced under ITA s.247.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 31 / Form T661 - SR&ED Investment Tax Credit and Expenditure Claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for qualified SR&ED expenditures on systematic experimental development of battery safety and UN38.3 drop-test methods; current-expenditure pool at 100% and capital pool on prescribed bases; federal ITC at 15% or 35% (enhanced CCPC rate on qualifying expenditures up to CAD 3,000,000)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SR&ED may only be claimed for work performed in Canada; allocate salaries, subcontractor fees, and overhead on contemporaneous time logs; the non-resident's Quebec PE must keep a complete technical narrative before filing the claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 400 / Schedule 1 - Part I tax computation and Line 700 Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after applying prior-year non-capital losses (20-year carryforward) and deductions under Part I; Part I tax at 15% reduced by the 10% provincial tax abatement and the general rate reduction, then Schedule 5 provincial allocation to Quebec
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations claim the provincial abatement only for income allocated to a Canadian PE; foreign tax credits on Schedule 125 are available for foreign-source income and must be reconciled with the treaty residence test.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty under ITA s.162(1): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of delay, up to 12 months (maximum 17%); repeat-filing penalty of 10% plus 2% per month; arrears and instalment interest compounded daily at the prescribed rate; gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2) of 50% of the understated tax.
